app.name: Atelier Inventory
app.tagline: Your dresses, photos and stock in one place.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: How the app works
help.whatBody: An inventory for a bridal atelier. Every dress, veil and jumpsuit has a code, a name, photographs, fabrics, prices and a status (available, reserved, rented, sold). Staff use it on a tablet on the shop floor; the owner uses it from a laptop.
help.startBody1: Sign in with the email and password the owner gave you. If you are staff, you can add dresses, take photographs, record movements and look up customers. Settings and user management are admin-only.
help.startBody2: The bottom bar has five tabs: Home (counts and quick actions), Dresses (the gallery and table), Capture (take photographs), Materials (fabrics and trims) and Account (sign out, language, theme).
help.dressesBody1: Dresses shows every garment as cards. Tap one to open it. Tap the plus button to add a new one: fill in the code (or let the app suggest one), the name, the category, the status, the listing (sale, rent or both) and the prices.
help.dressesBody2: Switch to the table view for a spreadsheet-like list with sortable columns and bulk actions. You can change the status of several dresses at once, or export them.
help.dressesBody3: To delete a dress, open it and tap Delete twice. The dress is soft-deleted and can be restored for a few seconds from the undo snackbar.
help.categoriesBody: Every garment is one of five kinds: wedding dress, party dress, engagement dress, veil or jumpsuit. The category is set on the form, can be filtered on the dresses page, and is shown on the printed catalogue, the stock report and the public card. The AI suggests a category from the photographs.
help.photosBody1: Open a dress and use the photo gallery, or use the Capture tab to take several at once. The app asks for the rear camera; you can flip to the front camera. It waits until the picture is sharp before saving, so a black frame is never stored.
help.photosBody2: Each dress keeps three angles: front, back and detail. The catalogue uses all three when they exist.
help.materialsBody: Fabrics, lace, trims, beads and so on. Each has a category, a quantity and a unit. Materials are linked to dresses so you know what a gown is made of and what to reorder.
help.customersBody: A customer record holds a name, phone, measurements and a history of movements. Start typing a name or phone to find one. Measurements are saved per customer and reused on the next visit.
help.movementsBody1: A movement is a rental or a sale. Open a dress and tap Check out (rent) or Sell. The dress status changes and the movement is recorded with the customer, the dates and the price.
help.movementsBody2: Check in returns a rented dress. Reserve holds it for a customer without taking it out of stock.
help.movementsBody3: Every movement prints a receipt and can be exported.
help.exportBody1: Dresses can be exported as Excel or CSV from the dresses page. The Excel file is a real spreadsheet: prices are numbers, dates are dates, the header is frozen and the atelier logo is on it.
help.exportBody2: The printed catalogue, the stock report, the hang tag and the tag sheet are PDFs. The catalogue carries the cover, the photographs, the description and a QR code per dress. The stock report is a one-page summary with counts and a table.
help.exportBody3: All exports are in English, whatever language the app is in.
help.publicBody1: Every dress has a QR code on its hang tag. A customer scanning it opens a public page showing the dress photograph, the name and the description. No prices, no stock status.
help.publicBody2: The page is turned on or off from Settings. The QR carries an unguessable token, not the dress code, so the catalogue cannot be enumerated.
help.settingsBody1: Branding: the atelier name, tagline, contact line and logo. These appear on the printed documents and the public page.
help.settingsBody2: Tools and APIs: connect the AI (Gemini, free tier), the background remover, and ERPNext. Each integration is tested before it is saved.
help.settingsBody3: The ERP sync sends dresses to ERPNext. It needs an ERPNext server reachable from the atelier network; see the setup note the developer left.
help.cameraBody1: The app uses the rear camera by default and lets you flip to the front. It waits for a real frame before saving, so a black frame is never stored. If the camera is taken by another app, a retry button appears.
help.cameraBody2: For best results, photograph in good light, fill the frame with the dress, and take front, back and detail shots.
help.faq1: Q: Where is my data stored? A: In the cloud (Supabase). Nothing is stored on the tablet. If the tablet breaks, sign in from any browser and everything is there.
help.faq2: Q: Does it work offline? A: The screens you have already opened work offline. Saving a new dress or taking a photograph needs a connection.
help.faq3: Q: How do I change my password? A: Account screen, then use the password reset link sent to your email. Ask the owner if you do not have access to that mailbox.

branding.hint: The name and logo printed on the hang tags and the catalogue, and shown on the public page a customer reaches by scanning the QR code.
